context.why: The last story: community managers maintain the profiles nobody else can sign in to fix. US1 and US2 are accepted on this branch: is_editable_by on Person (self only) and Organization (active keepers only), both forms, the Update page, both overviews wired for the record's own keepers, seed accounts for an owner, administrator, member and former administrator. This story adds the community manager branch to both rules, PortalRoles.is_held_by, the edit action a community manager sees, two seed accounts, the administrator documentation, the one-table test of every account against every profile (SC-003), and two fixes found in US2 (T019, T020).
prior_decisions: decisions.md D2, D3, D4, D10 and every entry US1 and US2 wrote (D11 onward). Read them.

plan D1, the Person bullet, is the rule and it was corrected by the design review: a community manager may edit a person only when the account is inactive, or the person is not claimed AND has never signed in (last_login is None). account_state alone is not enough: createsuperuser and signup without email verification leave an active, signed-in account unmarked as claimed, and such a person must be editable by themself only. T013 tests that case by name.

PortalRoles.is_held_by(user, role): an authenticated, active user in the group named role.name. A superuser in no group does not hold it. Portal Administrators hold contributors.change_person and still get nothing here: never test the Django permission.

Organization page for an editor who does not keep the record (can_edit and not can_manage): a single 'Edit details' button, no menu, no checklist. A community manager who is also the organization's administrator sees the menu only: exactly one edit link either way.
Person page for a community manager on an editable profile: the same 'Edit profile' button the person would see, and no checklist. The Contact stand-in stays as it is.
The editing page's line about where email, password and sign-ins are managed is shown only on your own profile (is_own_profile), so a community manager does not see it.

Scenario 5 (the profile is claimed, or the account reactivated, between opening and saving): the POST gets 403 and nothing is stored. Plugin re-runs the check on POST; test it, do not build a second mechanism.

Seed accounts: community-manager.user@example.com and data-curator.user@example.com, password `password`, holding those roles, added the way US2 added PROFILE_ACCOUNTS in demo/seed/common.py. fairdm.E501 must report them.
T019: strip a leading https://ror.org/ before matching in Organization.clean, nothing more. Do not change what update_identifier stores.
T020: guard each place a form's __init__ or save reads a field that a subclass may have dropped.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the users and profiles in tasks.md T013, when is_held_by and is_editable_by are asked, then they answer as listed, and the Data Curator's declared permissions are unchanged.
Given US-3 scenarios 1 to 11, when the real pages are opened and submitted, then each Then holds; a save refused mid-edit stores nothing.
Given the failing tests from T013 and T014, when the implementation lands, then all pass with no migration.
Given a development environment, when seed_profiles runs, then the two role accounts exist and hold their roles; the administrator guide says who may edit profiles; the docs step passes.
Given each seeded kind of account and each kind of profile, when the editing page is requested with GET and POST, then it opens exactly where FR-001 to FR-003a say and is refused everywhere else.
Given an organization whose ROR is stored as a full address, when full_clean runs, then it passes; a malformed ROR still fails.
Given a subclass of a shipped form without languages, website or parent, when it is built and saved, then it works.
